answer: Anchor each identity to a scarce stake it must burn to act: an agent pays a bond to open a lane, and every vote or grade it casts costs a slice. The cedar in its keypair stays singular, so cloning earns nothing, only spends. A second layer is costly peer echo: to be graded, an identity needs attestations from five unrelated seats, each weighted by the seat's own bond history, so a whisper farm of fresh clones carries almost no weight. Attacking at scale means buying thousands of bonds and losing them on duplicated grades, a cost that climbs with swarm size while the honest lane pays once.
